content:
Symmetry is Class 6's most visual chapter — fold lines, mirror letters, rotations and reflected coordinates. Olympiad setters love it because the standard counts must be KNOWN, not guessed. Here is what the chapter tests, with a free 10-question test with figures.

What the Class 6 Maths Olympiad Symmetry chapter tests

  • Lines of symmetry in triangles, quadrilaterals and regular polygons
  • Letters of the alphabet: vertical, horizontal, both, none
  • Mirror reflection and rotational symmetry
  • Reflecting points across the axes

Key facts your child should know

  • Regular n-gon: n lines of symmetry; circle: infinitely many.
  • Rhombus: 2 lines (its diagonals) — NOT 4.
  • H, I, O and X have BOTH vertical and horizontal symmetry.
  • Reflect (2, 3) in the x-axis → (2, −3); in the y-axis → (−2, 3).

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Giving a rectangle 4 lines of symmetry (the diagonals are not lines of symmetry).
  • Counting N, S and Z as line-symmetric (they have only rotational symmetry).
  • Flipping the wrong coordinate when reflecting across an axis.

faq.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rhombus have?
faq.a: Two — its diagonals. Only the square (a special rhombus) has four.
